A critical bug was found: `executeGroup` passes `document: doc.uri`, but `runSingleHandler` checks `args.document` first and incorrectly treats it as a `NotebookCell`.

The handler treats the URI as a single cell. `executeOneEnhancedCell` then crashes because it expects a `NotebookCell` with a numeric index and cell methods, but receives a URI instead.

The regression stems from two new helpers: `executeGroup` and `executeNotebookCell` both pass `document: doc.uri`. Previously `executeGroup` only sent `{ ranges: targetCells }`, so the handler correctly fell through to the ranges branch. Adding `document` broke that path and triggered the faulty single-cell logic.

A secondary edge case was noted: `runSingleHandler` resolves the notebook from the active editor rather than `args.document`, so the wrong notebook could still be targeted if the user has a different notebook focused. This may be pre-existing. The main new bug remains the `document` plus `ranges` ambiguity.

The `document` field in `executeGroup` signals intent to target a specific notebook, but `runSingleHandler` ignores it entirely. This creates a medium-severity edge case where the active editor is used instead of the intended notebook, risking execution of the wrong cells if their indices differ.

The old `runSequenceHandler` re-registered both hijacks inside a `try/finally` block. The new code removes that cleanup and only re-registers the single hijack via `withNativeCellExecute`. The outer `allHijack` for `notebook.execute` remains active throughout the sequence. This change may leave the outer hijack unregistered if the single hijack is disposed mid-sequence.

The old `runSequenceHandler` re-registered both hijacks inside a `try/finally` block. The new code removes that cleanup and relies on per-cell `withNativeCellExecute` registration instead. This should be safe for the sequence handler.

Concurrent `executeGroup` calls are properly serialized by `executeGate`. Each cell in the multi-cell loop also gets its own `withNativeCellExecute` wrapper, so execution ordering remains correct.

The hijacked `runSingleHandler` executes the full multi-cell loop internally, so the outer `executeGroup` call does not go through `withNativeCellExecute`. `executeGroup` now awaits the async hijacked handler, ensuring it waits until all cells finish.

The success message in `allNotebookTagsTreeDataProvider` still reads "Executing" after `executeGroup` finishes, though this appears to be a pre-existing style quirk rather than a new bug.

A deeper issue remains: the `args.document` check cannot reliably distinguish a real `NotebookCell` from a notebook URI. Both carry a `.document` property, so the handler must inspect other fields like `.index`, `.kind`, or `.notebook` to determine whether it is processing a single cell or a multi-cell group.

The handler should check for `args.ranges` before treating `args.document` as a notebook URI. This cleanly separates native cell objects from multi-cell groups. The `executeCellAndWaitNative` helper uses `notebookUri` directly, so it remains safe when the single hijack is disposed. Re-entrant calls during native execution are handled correctly.

A concurrency risk was identified. If two `runSingleHandler` executions overlap, the second can hit the hijack while the first is still running. Because `executeGate` only serializes individual `withNativeCellExecute` calls, the outer multi-cell loop between cells is not protected. This allows cells from both groups to interleave.

The concurrency bug is newly introduced. Previously `executeGroup` only ran the first cell, so the hijack was never active between cells. Now the sequential multi-cell loop re-registers the hijack after each cell, leaving the handler exposed during the 100ms delay and animation between cells. Another `executeGroup` call can therefore start a parallel `runSingleHandler` that interleaves cells from both groups.

A double-call bug was spotted in `handleCellFinished`. `executeOneEnhancedCell` invokes it directly, and `handleExecutionStateChange` may invoke it again when the cell state becomes idle. This likely existed before the current changes.

A new bug was found in `summaryLooksComplete`. The function now requires `success !== undefined` to mark completion, but it no longer checks `endChanged`. This means a stale `success` value from a previous run could prematurely signal completion before the current execution actually ends.

The `summaryLooksComplete` logic is more dangerous than it first appeared. Because `orderChanged` sets `sawStarted` to true, the next poll sees `sawStarted` as true and `success` as defined. Without `endChanged`, the function returns `success` immediately. This can cause a stale summary value to signal completion while the cell is still executing.

The `summaryLooksComplete` regression is confirmed as a logic bug. When a new execution begins, VS Code updates `executionOrder` but may not clear the old `success` value. The new poll then sees `success` defined and `sawStarted` true, returning the stale result prematurely. This causes `executeCellAndWaitNative` to resolve too early for kernels that update the order without setting `endTime`.

The `anchorIndex` assignment in `runSequenceHandler` was tightened. The old code assumed `args.document` meant a cell object, but the new check `typeof args.index === 'number'` correctly handles both cell objects and multi-cell groups that lack an index.

The `executeGroup` path always falls back to the active editor when no cell is provided, so the wrong notebook is targeted whenever the active editor differs from the intended one. This appears to be a pre-existing bug rather than a new regression.

A critical scoping bug was identified. When `executeGroup` receives a cell argument, it resolves the target notebook from that cell but still runs the hijacked handler against the active editor's cells. If the active editor belongs to a different notebook, the ranges resolve against the wrong notebook entirely. This mismatch likely existed before the recent changes, since earlier versions also lacked explicit notebook scoping.

The scoping mismatch in `executeGroup` is pre-existing, not newly introduced. The old loop executed the entire group once per cell reference, which was wasteful but not a logic error. The new code correctly calls `executeGroup` once per tag, fixing that inefficiency.

The VS Code native format uses the notebook URI as `document`, not a cell URI.

The hijack would break normal VS Code runs too. When VS Code passes the standard options object `{ranges, document}`, the first branch treats the entire object as a single cell. This means the handler is broken for both manual and automatic execution unless VS Code occasionally passes a raw Cell object instead.

Normal toolbar runs likely hit the selection fallback branch when args are empty, so those still work. The bug only triggers during automated execution where executeGroup explicitly passes `{ranges, document}`. Previously executeGroup only sent `{ranges}`, which matched the correct branch and worked by accident.

Adding `document` to the executeGroup call is the exact change that introduced the regression. The handler should check for `args.ranges` first, then fall back to a NotebookCell check, then to the selection fallback. Currently `args && args.document` matches the options object and misroutes execution.

## document field blocks ranges parsing

`src/jupyterEnhancements/extension.ts:344-367` · Severity: high

<details open>
<summary>Description</summary>

`runSingleHandler` treats any args with a `document` property as a `NotebookCell`, but `executeGroup` and `executeNotebookCell` now invoke `notebook.cell.execute` with the native `{ ranges, document: notebookUri }` options shape. The handler takes the single-cell branch with the options object itself, ignores `ranges`, and calls `executeOneEnhancedCell` on a non-cell (typically throwing on `cell.notebook`), so Execute Tag Run Group and Run Tag do not run tagged cells.

</details>

## Stale success completes execution early

`src/jupyterEnhancements/extension.ts:520-523` · Severity: high

<details open>
<summary>Description</summary>

The new `summaryLooksComplete` branch returns `summary.success` whenever `sawStarted`, `orderChanged`, and `success` are all set, without requiring `timing.endTime` to change. On re-execution, `executionSummary.success` often still reflects the previous run when the execution order updates, so `executeCellAndWaitNative` can resolve before the new run finishes.

</details>
